definitions.explanation: A seven-day Buddhist memorial period centered on the spring and autumn equinoxes, when Japanese people traditionally visit family graves and make offerings to ancestors.

examples.japanese: お{彼岸|ひがん}に{墓参|はかまい}りをする。
examples.english: We visit the grave during higan.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}のお{彼岸|ひがん}には{牡丹餅|ぼたもち}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: We make botamochi (rice cakes) for spring higan.

examples.japanese: お{彼岸|ひがん}の{時期|じき}になると、スーパーに{供|そな}え{物|もの}が{並|なら}ぶ。
examples.english: When higan season comes, offerings are displayed at supermarkets.

notes:
お{彼岸|ひがん} is a Japanese Buddhist observance period.

SEASONS:
- {春|はる}のお{彼岸|ひがん}: Spring higan (around March 20-21)
- {秋|あき}のお{彼岸|ひがん}: Autumn higan (around September 22-23)

TRADITIONAL FOODS:
- {牡丹餅|ぼたもち}: Spring rice cakes (named after peony flowers)
- {御萩|おはぎ}: Autumn rice cakes (named after bush clover)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The equinox is considered a time when the boundary between this world and the afterlife is thinnest. Families visit graves ({墓参|はかまい}り), clean tombstones, and make offerings of flowers and food. The expression 「{暑|あつ}さ{寒|さむ}さも{彼岸|ひがん}まで」 means extreme heat and cold end around the equinoxes.
